name: Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam
tagline: Navy and Air Force on Oahu's south shore, where Pearl Harbor and Hickam joined in 2010.
_note: Hawaii joint base (Naval Station Pearl Harbor + Hickam AFB, merged 2010), Oahu. Marked OCONUS (a Hawaii PCS is an overseas-style move) but BAH-rated: MHA HI408 (Honolulu County) via the bah_rates single source of truth, so the full live template stays. Facts verified from official sources (cnic.navy.mil, housing.af.mil, tripler.tricare.mil, DeCA/NEX, Wikipedia for corroborated headline facts). Housing via Ohana Military Communities (Navy, Hunt) and Hickam Communities (Air Force, Centinel); re-verified 2026-11-10, including Red Hill (EPA final assessment, March 2026). No DoDEA in Hawaii (Hawaii State DOE). Medium-confidence flags: base coords (approx), representative off-base ZIP 96818 (Honolulu).

sections.title: Mission & Identity
data: Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam was formed on Oct. 1, 2010, when Naval Station Pearl Harbor integrated with Hickam Air Force Base. It is the larger of Navy Region Hawaii's two installations, with more than 270 tenant commands (2022).
It hosts Commander, U.S. Pacific Fleet, the Pacific submarine force, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Pacific Air Forces headquarters, the 15th Wing and the Hawaii Air National Guard's 154th Wing.

sections.title: An Island Assignment: Cost, Housing, and the Aloha Trade-offs

data.subtitle: Hawaii is paradise and a logistical puzzle. BAH is high but the cost of living is higher, housing is tight, and an island PCS comes with quirks (shipping a car, limited space) that reward planning early.
intro: A Hawaii tour is a true OCONUS-style move even though it's a U.S. state: you ship household goods by sea, can usually bring only one vehicle at government expense, and everything imported costs more. Hawaii also pays a cost-of-living allowance on top of BAH.

Where you live trades commute against cost: Aiea is about 7 minutes from Nimitz Gate with no traffic, Kapolei about 23 and Ewa Beach about 29, and Skyline rail now runs from East Kapolei to the base's Makalapa station. In Hawaii your address also sets your children's school.

Red Hill: in November 2021 a fuel release from the Red Hill Bulk Fuel Storage Facility contaminated the Red Hill Shaft, a Navy drinking water well, affecting about 93,000 people. Unrestricted drinking water use returned in March 2022, and as of September 2026 the Red Hill Shaft remained disconnected. A Defense Department task force finished draining the facility's bulk fuel (about 104.7 million gallons) in March 2024; cleanup continues, and the Navy plans to close the facility in 2028.

recommendations.advice: Apply before you leave with HEAT. Ohana Military Communities (Navy, managed by Hunt) and Hickam Communities (Air Force, a Centinel community) each give their own service priority, and many neighborhoods are near full on arrival. Navy housing bills utilities under the Resident Energy Conservation Program.

Kapolei and Ewa Beach had typical home values of about $841,000 and $832,000 in September 2026 (Zillow) and are about 23 to 29 minutes from Nimitz Gate with no traffic; Skyline rail links East Kapolei to the base.
Arrange your one-vehicle shipment, expect a sea shipment for household goods, and budget for a higher cost of living than the BAH suggests.

EPA concluded in March 2026 that the water affected by the 2021 Red Hill fuel release has been free of fuel contamination and in compliance since 2022, and the Hawaii Department of Health agreed. The Navy posts test results at jbphh-safewaters.org.

source.label: U.S. EPA, 2021 JBPHH drinking water incident (official)

sections.title: Gates & Access
data: Gates include Nimitz Gate, Makalapa Gate and Kuntz Gate. We found no official list of gate hours, so ask your sponsor or command which gate suits your shift.

The Pass and ID Office is in Bldg. 3455 by Nimitz Gate, weekdays 6 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. (noon every third Thursday), (808) 449-0865. Since May 6, 2025 only REAL ID-compliant licenses and ID cards are accepted, and sponsors must submit the request in person and stay with their guests in the Pass and ID Office until the pass is issued; no phone requests.

source.label: Nimitz Visitor Control Center, Pass and ID (official)

sections.title: On-Base Housing
data: Base housing is two separate privatized projects. Navy housing is Ohana Military Communities, managed by Hunt Military Communities (4,435 homes, per Military OneSource); Air Force housing is Hickam Communities, a Centinel Public Partnerships community (2,484 homes on Hickam). Each gives its own service first priority.

Many neighborhoods are near full on arrival, and some families rent off base while they wait. Apply before you leave with HEAT, and report within 72 hours of arrival: Navy Housing Service Center, 4825 Bougainville Dr, 808-474-1820; Air Force Housing Management Office, 200 Kokomalei St, 808-312-0199. Navy housing bills utilities under the Resident Energy Conservation Program.

source.label: DoD 2026 BAH Rates, MHA HI408 (Honolulu County)

sections.title: Schools
data: Hawaii runs a single statewide public school system (the Hawaii State Department of Education), and there are no DoD schools in Hawaii; your school is assigned by your home address, and you can't enroll before you have one.

Base housing is served by Mokulele, Hickam, Aliamanu, Pearl Harbor Kai, Pearl Harbor and Nimitz elementary schools, and Aliamanu Middle feeds Radford High; confirm the schools for your neighborhood. In 2025-26 Radford's students were 63% proficient in language arts and 34% in math, with a 94% graduation rate (class of 2025).

Requests to attend a different school (geographic exceptions) are due January 1 to March 1 for the next school year, and approval depends on space. School Liaison Office: 530 Peltier Ave, Bldg. 1925, 808-306-9247, JBPHHSLO@us.navy.mil.

source.label: Hawaii DOE military families; 2025-26 Strive HI reports (official)

intro: Whether to rent or buy is the biggest money decision of most PCS moves. In Hawaii it leans toward renting or living on base for most families, because home prices are among the highest in the country and tours are usually a fixed length.
rent: Your tour is a standard length and your orders feel fixed.
Island home prices are out of reach for your budget, which is common.
On-base housing offers a strong value against high island rents.
You'd rather not manage a high-priced home from afar after you leave.
buy: You expect a long tour or plan to return to or retire in Hawaii.
You can carry Hawaii's high prices and want to build equity with your VA loan.
You're comfortable potentially renting it out at island rates later.
You've found a home and commute you're confident about.
data.bottom_line: There is no universal right answer, but high prices and fixed tours make on-base or renting the common choice in Hawaii. Run your BAH against the rent and home prices above, factor the higher cost of living, and talk to a lender and an agent who work with military families before you commit.

intro: An island PCS has extra logistics. Knocking these out early makes everything else easier.

steps.title: Line up temporary lodging
steps.text: Book on-base lodging or a short-term rental before you arrive. You can claim Temporary Lodging Allowance (TLA) for OCONUS-style moves; confirm the current rules.

steps.title: In-process and update DEERS
steps.text: Report to your command and finance, and make sure DEERS and ID cards are current for every family member so TRICARE and base access work.

steps.title: Get on the housing list early
steps.text: Apply before you leave with HEAT, then report within 72 hours of arrival: Navy members to the Navy Housing Service Center (808-474-1820), Air Force members to an in-person Housing Management Office appointment (808-312-0199).

steps.title: Sort your vehicle and shipment
steps.text: Track your sea shipment of household goods and your one shipped vehicle; arrange interim transportation and Hawaii registration.

steps.title: Enroll the kids in school
steps.text: Hawaii uses one statewide system; confirm your assigned school by address and bring records and immunizations.

steps.title: Set up healthcare
steps.text: Update your TRICARE enrollment so you can be seen at Tripler Army Medical Center or a base clinic.

data.a: Yes. Even though Hawaii is a U.S. state, a PCS here works like an overseas move: you ship household goods by sea, usually ship one vehicle, and receive island allowances. You still get BAH (not OHA), set by Honolulu County.

It depends on availability: many neighborhoods are near full on arrival, so some families rent off base while they wait. Apply before you leave with HEAT. Ohana Military Communities (Navy, managed by Hunt) and Hickam Communities (Air Force, a Centinel community) each give their own service priority.

Tripler Army Medical Center is the only military treatment facility on Oahu with an emergency room. On base are Naval Health Clinic Hawaii's clinics (including BHC Makalapa) and the 15th Medical Group at Hickam, which has no emergency room.
JBPHH is MHA HI408 (Honolulu County). Use the calculator above for your grade.
